title: Milo Yiannopoulos deported after ICE arrest and detention at major Louisiana removal hub
summary: Milo Yiannopoulos was arrested at a Louisiana airport and deported after DHS says he overstayed his visa and skipped an immigration hearing.
story: Jonathan Fahey, former DHS deputy assistant secretary, discusses Democratic opposition to deploying ICE agents at airports. He criticizes Chicago's sanctuary city policy after an illegal Venezuelan migrant, Jose Medina-Medina, was charged with the murder of an 18-year-old woman.
Controversial former Breitbart editor Milo Yiannopoulos was deported to the United Kingdom one day after ICE agents arrested him at a Louisiana airport.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said he overstayed his welcome in the United States and skipped an immigration hearing.

In a new statement, the DHS said Immigration and Customs Enforcement deported Yiannopoulos Friday, one day after agents arrested the British national at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport in Kenner, Louisiana.
Yiannopoulos was then held in ICE custody in Alexandria, Louisiana, a major hub for the agency’s deportation operations, before his removal from the country.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PLANS NEW ICE HOLDING FACILITY NEAR LOUISIANA DEPORTATION FLIGHT HUB
In this Feb. 21, 2017 photo, Milo Yiannopoulos speaks during a news conference in New York.  (Lucas Jackson/Reuters)
DHS said Yiannopoulos legally entered the United States through New York City May 14, 2019, but remained after his authorized stay expired.
An immigration judge issued him a final order of removal on July 22 after he failed to appear for his immigration hearing, according to the agency.
"Yiannopoulos legally entered the country on May 14, 2019, through New York City, New York. He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws," DHS said.
BIDEN JUDGE OVERRULED ON KEY TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICY
Milo Yiannopoulos walks while being escorted away after speaking at the University of California in Berkeley. (Stephen Lam/Reuters/File)
The agency used Yiannopoulos’ removal to issue a broader warning to illegal immigrants and tout the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement policies.

DHS said it reversed a Biden administration policy that it claimed allowed illegal immigrants to fly around the country, adding that the department will no longer permit such travel unless it is tied to a departure from the United States.
DHS ISSUES $84B IN FINES TO ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS UNDER TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

"Under President Trump, DHS will no longer tolerate this," the agency said. "This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport."
DHS urged illegal immigrants to use the CBP Home app to arrange their own departures, saying the federal government is offering $3,000 and a free flight to those who leave voluntarily.
DHS HITS BACK AT JAMES TALARICO AFTER DEMOCRAT CLAIMS ICE 'KIDNAPPED' 5-YEAR-OLD BOY DEPORTED WITH FATHER
Far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos holds protest signs while speaking at the University of California in Berkeley, Calif. Sept. 24, 2017.
"Being in detention is a choice," DHS said, adding that people who use the app may preserve a chance to return to the United States legally in the future.
Those who do not leave voluntarily, the agency warned, will be arrested and deported without a chance to return.
ICE ARRESTS SOUTHWEST AIRLINES FLIGHT ATTENDANT IN NASHVILLE FOR ALLEGEDLY OVERSTAYING VISA SINCE 2021

Yiannopoulos rose to national prominence as a provocative political commentator and former editor at Breitbart News. He drew national attention for his provocative speeches and online commentary, including appearances that sparked protests at UC Berkeley.

summary: Mica Miller's siblings allege JP Miller had her involuntarily committed as part of a coercive control pattern during their troubled marriage.
story: South Carolina woman Mica Miller, found dead in Lumber River State Park on April 27, called 911 in the moments before her death, according to the Robeson County Sheriff's Office. (Credit: Robeson County Sheriff's Office)
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Mica Miller's siblings are speaking out about the late worship leader's troubled marriage, alleging her estranged husband, South Carolina pastor John-Paul "JP" Miller, had her involuntarily admitted to a mental health center.

Mica’s family discusses the alleged hospitalization in "Death of the Pastor’s Wife," a three-part true-crime series that premiered Wednesday on Netflix. The documentary delves into her life, marriage and April 2024 death, which authorities ruled a suicide.
Mica’s family describes the hospitalization as part of a broader alleged pattern of coercive control during her marriage.
SC PASTOR'S WIFE MICA MILLER TOLD POLICE SHE WAS BEING TRACKED BEFORE HER SUICIDE: DOCS

Mica Miller was found dead in the water with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, and the gun was located nearby April 27. 2024. The North Carolina Medical Examiner’s Office later ruled the death a suicide. (Courtesy of Netflix)

John-Paul Miller and Mica Miller and John-Paul Miller, right, after an arrest. (Facebook)
In a handwritten affidavit accompanying her divorce filing reviewed by Fox News Digital, Mica alleged that she had been abused "emotionally, sexually, spiritually, financially, and physically."

The family further said that while Mica was hospitalized, Miller took possession of her vehicle, phone and laptop. Her siblings said the computer contained intimate photographs of her. Mica later reported the alleged incident to police, according to the Netflix series.

title: Strange Georgia crime scene clues blow hole in theory of mom’s mysterious death, family says
summary: Natalie Jones' toxicology report came back clean, yet Georgia authorities pushed an overdose theory before closing her 2020 Heard County death case.
story: Internet searches from conman Brian Walshe and voicemails from his mother, Diana, take center stage in new Fox Nation special on the Ana Walshe murder case.
A negative toxicology report, missing teeth and an unusually positioned driver’s seat are fueling renewed questions into the unexplained 2020 death of Georgia mother Natalie Jones.
"The Truth About Natalie," a six-part Audiochuck series, examines the 27-year-old’s life before her disappearance, the circumstances surrounding her death and a questionable overdose theory.
The series draws from case files, crime scene evidence, candid interviews with family members and a volunteer advocate, along with independent forensic analysis.
Jones’ mother, Elaine Gordon, told Fox News Digital that friction with investigators began during the search. She alleged that a detective accused her of interfering as she pressed for answers.
Natalie Jones was found dead in Georgia in 2020. (Courtesy of Elaine Gordon)
DETECTIVES' TRUE-CRIME PODCAST TAKES FRESH SHOT AT KILLER WHO VANISHED AFTER CAUGHT-ON-CAMERA MURDER

"What did they expect me to do, sit at home and be quiet? And I still want somebody to answer this for me: How do we even know Natalie left that lake house in the first place?" Gordon told Fox News Digital.
Gordon also questioned whether investigators thoroughly interviewed everyone connected to her daughter’s final hours.
The final text
Jones disappeared after reportedly leaving a friend’s lake house in Jackson’s Gap, Alabama, July 4, 2020, in a bright pink 2002 Chevrolet Cavalier. She planned to drive home to Heard County, Georgia.
At 12:52 a.m. the following morning, her phone sent its last outgoing text to the mother of a former boyfriend.
Natalie Jones' family wants answers as questions remain about how she died in Georgia. (Courtesy of Elaine Gordon)
"I made it. Thanks."
The message did not indicate where Jones had arrived.

Cellphone data reviewed in the podcast indicated that, on July 5, Jones’ phone connected with towers across Heard County in a scattered pattern, including on the opposite side of the county from her home. Cellular activity stopped shortly after 5 a.m.
Later that morning, Jones failed to arrive at her sister’s home to babysit her children, prompting the family to contact police.
Nearly three months passed without answers. Then, in October 2020, a property owner’s nephew discovered Jones’ vehicle off Roosterville Road in rural Heard County covered in thick vegetation.
Natalie Jones with one of her sons (Courtesy of Elaine Gordon)
UC DAVIS FRATERNITY STUDENT'S 2001 DEATH RULED A SUICIDE AFTER 29 STAB WOUNDS QUESTIONED IN TRUE-CRIME PODCAST

Heard County Sheriff’s Office deputies found Jones deceased in the driver’s seat, slumped toward the driver’s side door, wearing the same clothes she had worn to the gathering. Her body showed advanced decomposition and partial mummification.
The medical examiner could not determine Jones’ cause or manner of death.
GOLDEN STATE KILLER INVESTIGATOR FINDS ‘RED FLAGS’ IN MARILYN MONROE DEATH SCENE DECADES LATER
Questions inside the car
Although investigators said they found no evidence of foul play, the podcast highlighted several details that left Jones’ family scrambling for answers.

Crime scene photos showed the driver’s seat reclined and pushed farther back than Jones, who stood 5 feet, 5 inches tall, would have kept it. Strands of her hair were wedged along the driver-side door jamb, and the vehicle’s trunk had been popped open.
Natalie Jones was 27 when she died. (Courtesy of Elaine Gordon)
Jones’ cellphone, rhinestone sandals, belt and white sunglasses were unaccounted for. Several of her teeth were also missing.
Investigators found a small bag inside the car, possibly containing methamphetamine, but the GBI Crime Lab recovered no fingerprints from it. Jones’ toxicology screening came back negative for drugs.
Family seeks new review

In 2021, family advocate Jennifer Peterson petitioned the Heard County Superior Court to impanel a special grand jury to examine Jones’ death, including the possible involvement of a former boyfriend who had been identified as a person of interest, but never charged in the case.
In 2022, the district attorney told Peterson that the case was being closed.
"We have raised serious questions, inconsistencies and concerns, and too often it feels like they are dismissed, minimized or ignored," Peterson told Fox News Digital.
By 2023, law enforcement and the district attorney’s office had stopped responding to her, Peterson said.
Natalie Jones wanted a better life for herself and her two sons, her mother said. (Courtesy of Elaine Gordon)
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"At some point, you have to ask, ‘Who polices the police?’ And what does it take for someone with the authority to simply say, ‘I’ll listen, I’ll look at it, and I’ll help?’ We are still waiting for that person. Hopefully, someone can help us."
Peterson contacted Audiochuck podcast host Sean Kipe in March 2023.
"What bothers me most is that authorities pushed an accidental overdose theory even though Natalie’s toxicology report came back completely clean," Kipe told Fox News Digital.
"Combining that negative drug test with missing evidence like her phone, shoes and teeth makes it nearly impossible to accept the official explanation."
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Kipe said Heard County authorities have not contacted him since the podcast’s release. He added, however, that several law enforcement officers from the area reached out to him with doubts about the overdose theory.
The Heard County Sheriff’s Office told Fox News Digital that investigators are still seeking leads in the case and that if "anything comes in, we will be glad to run it down."
The Heard County DA’s Office referred the inquiry to the West Georgia Judicial Circuit DA’s Office, which was not immediately available for comment.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
"My ultimate hope is to bring Natalie’s mother and children the closure they deserve after years of unanswered questions," Kipe said.
SEND US A TIP
"By sharing this story with a wide audience, we want to compel authorities to reopen the investigation into Natalie’s death and encourage anyone with information about the case to come forward."
GOT A TIP?
Natalie Jones is pictured with her mother, Elaine Gordon. (Courtesy of Elaine Gordon)
For Gordon, the podcast also offers an opportunity to show listeners who her daughter was beyond the unanswered questions surrounding her death.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
"I want everybody to know how loved Natalie was and how much she loved her boys, Trent and Isaac. She wanted a better life for the three of them," Gordon said. "She was excited about her future."
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Gordon said that, before she disappeared, Jones had bought land and was planning to build a home there for her two young sons. She also had plans to attend college.

title: Fox Hollow coroner reveals why he doubts suspected serial killer acted alone in hunt for answers
summary: Over 9,000 bones remain unexamined at Fox Hollow Farm as the true crime documentary explores whether suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister acted alone.
story: The Indiana coroner leading an investigation to identify the victims of the alleged Fox Hollow Farm serial killer said that "several tragedies" still remain.

Nearly 30 years after thousands of human bones and bone fragments were unearthed at the sprawling estate of suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister, new questions are being raised about the mystery of what really happened at Fox Hollow Farm.
The coroner leading the renewed investigation claims a key figure in the case has not been fully forthcoming with investigators.
"I have had an opportunity to speak with Mark Goodyear a couple of times," Hamilton County Coroner Jeff Jellison told Fox News Digital.
FOX HOLLOW FARM SERIAL KILLER'S 10TH VICTIM IDENTIFIED: CORONER
Hamilton County coroner Jeff Jellison's mission is to identify the remains from Fox Hollow Farm. (ABC News Studios)

"The first question I would ask him is, ‘Are you ready to be honest with me?’ Because in the conversations we’ve had, he’s not been honest. I’ve asked him questions that I knew the answer to, and he didn’t pass that test. So for me to sit down with Mark Goodyear, he’s going to have to be willing to be honest in this conversation. I don’t have time to sit down with somebody that tells lies, untruths."
Authorities dig for human bones in a wooded area on the Fox Hollow Farm in Westfield. (Rich Miller/Indy Star-USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn)

Jellison appears in the ABC News Studios true crime documentary "Return to Fox Hollow: New Victims, Darker Secrets," which explores new theories about potential accomplices, overlooked evidence and witness accounts in the case of Baumeister, a suspected serial killer believed to have murdered numerous men in Indiana. It's a follow-up to the 2025 docuseries "The Fox Hollow Murders: Playground of a Serial Killer."
Jellison said he wants to determine whether Goodyear knows something that could help investigators identify the remaining victims and determine how they died.
Indiana resident Herb Baumeister was suspected of killing at least 25 victims. (Indianapolis Police Department)
Goodyear has never been charged with any crime related to the case and has repeatedly denied any involvement in the disappearances.

"If we move forward in that conversation, certainly I want to know any information I can gather to help identify these remains," said Jellison. "Were you familiar with anybody? Things that would focus more around identification and how these people died."
A portrait of Jeffery Allen Jones, who was identified as a victim of suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister. (Michelle Pemberton/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn)
"Mark Goodyear knows a lot about this case," Jellison said.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Mark Goodyear was questioned by Hamilton County police in 1996. He claimed to be Herb Baumeister’s sole survivor. (ABC News Studios)
Jellison also shared that Goodyear knew many people through gay nightclubs and could help investigators identify some of the remains.

Goodyear, who participated in the first docuseries, has described himself as Baumeister's only known survivor. The film detailed how investigators believed Baumeister may have filmed his victims with a secret camera hidden in an air vent in his basement. Goodyear said he was forced to watch some of the tapes in 1994. He said the video was so "bad" it made him scream.
A memorial stands at Prairie Waters Funeral and Event Center at Hamilton Memorial Park for the victims of suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister. (Michelle Pemberton/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK)

"It was like having a camera right up against something," Goodyear said. "You're not going to be able to tell what's going on, but the minute you got a flash of what was going on, it made you scream."
"Return to Fox Hollow: New Victims, Darker Secrets" is available for streaming on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+. (ABC News Studios)

The previous documentary examined how Goodyear's account of his relationship and encounters with Baumeister has changed over the years. At the time, Jellison told Fox News Digital it was unlikely those tapes, if they exist, would ever be recovered.
Fox News Digital reached out to Goodyear for comment but did not receive a response.
Daniel Thomas Halloran's remains were identified after they were found at Fox Hollow Farm. (Michelle Pemberton/USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn and Hamilton County Coroner's Office)
Goodyear initially agreed to another interview for the follow-up documentary but did not appear for the scheduled interview, according to the film.
SIGN UP TO GET THE TRUE CRIME NEWSLETTER
Mark Goodyear did not participate in "Return to Fox Hollow: New Victims, Darker Secrets." He left a voicemail for producers heard in the film. (ABC News Studios)

About 10,000 burned and broken human bones and bone fragments were recovered from the 18-acre estate that once belonged to Baumeister. Before investigators could arrest him in 1996, Baumeister was found dead of a self-inflicted gunshot wound in Ontario, Canada. He was 49.

title: Bryan Kohberger seeks judge’s removal in escalating bid to undo guilty plea
summary: Bryan Kohberger is seeking to withdraw his guilty plea for the murders of four University of Idaho students, arguing he was coerced into a false confession.
story: Dr. Kris Mohandie, a renowned forensic psychologist who predicted Bryan Kohberger would attempt to appeal his guilty plea last year, weighs in on Kohberger's ‘narcissism’ and latest legal move.

Bryan Kohberger, the man convicted of fatally stabbing four University of Idaho students, is asking a court to disqualify the judge in his case and has asked for a change of venue as he attempts to take back his guilty plea.
Motions for both requests were filed Thursday by Kohberger's new court-appointed attorney, Gregory Rauch. The move came after Kohberger was convicted of first-degree murder.
Kohberger has since claimed he is innocent and has blamed his defense team for leading him to make a false confession.
BRYAN KOHBERGER GETS NEW ATTORNEY APPOINTED AFTER HE ASKS COURT FOR POST-CONVICTION RELIEF IN IDAHO MURDERS

Bryan Kohberger appears at the Ada County Courthouse for his sentencing hearing July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho, for brutally stabbing four University of Idaho students to death. (AP Photo/Kyle Green, Pool)

The motions are asking for Fourth Judicial District Judge Steven Hippler to be disqualified for Kohberger's post-conviction court proceedings and for the hearings to be moved out of Ada County. The motion to disqualify Hippler questions his impartiality.

"This motion does not rest upon one adverse ruling, one harsh statement, or the mere fact that the judge who presided over Bryan Kohberger’s criminal case has been assigned to his post-conviction proceeding," the motion states. "It rests upon the extraordinary convergence of all of them."

Although his original criminal trial was relocated to Ada County in 2024 to ensure an impartial jury and adequate resources, his lawyers argue those concerns are irrelevant to a bench proceeding decided solely by a judge.
BRYAN KOHBERGER'S POST-CONVICTION RELIEF BID ENABLED BY FLAWED PLEA DEAL, PSYCHOLOGIST ARGUES

Kohberger, 31, last year pleaded guilty to four counts of first-degree murder and a felony burglary charge for the 2022 stabbing deaths of University of Idaho students Madison Mogen, 21, Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, 20.
However, Kohberger is now asking to be granted a trial even though he could possibly face the death penalty.

The central pillar of the motion to remove the judge rests on the "constitutional adequacy" of the trial counsel's preparation. Defense lawyers argued the capital trial schedule made it impossible to review the massive amount of evidence in the case.
The defense cautioned the court that forcing it to proceed to trial under those conditions threatened Kohberger’s constitutional right to effective representation.
Hippler rejected the defense’s claims that it was unprepared for trial, accusing it of using the massive volume of discovery as a tactic for delay rather than a genuine concern.
KOHBERGER DEFENSE TEAM SAYS IT IS 'APPALLED' BY FORMER EXPERT'S PUBLIC COMMENTS ABOUT IDAHO MURDERS CASE
The motion also refers to Hippler's statement during sentencing in which he made pronouncements regarding Kohberger's ability to tell the truth.
"Do we really believe, after all of this, he is capable of speaking the truth?" he said, according to the document.
The judge also called Kohberger a "faceless coward" and the "the worst of the worst."

"Those statements are fundamentally different from believing Kohberger committed terrible crimes or deserved severe punishment," the motion states. "They are forward-looking judgments about his credibility. And credibility may now be at the center of this proceeding."

Madison Mogen, top left, smiles on the shoulders of her best friend, Kaylee Goncalves, as they pose with Ethan Chapin, Xana Kernodle and two other housemates in Goncalves' final Instagram post shared the day before the four students were stabbed to death. (@kayleegoncalves/Instagram)

"Transfer is warranted in a case like this where ‘the convenience of witnesses and the ends of justice would be promoted by the change,’" that motion states.

title: ICE officer charged in Minneapolis shooting released in Texas after judge declines to intervene

story: Fox News correspondent Christina Coleman reports from Dallas on a federal judge blocking attempts by Minnesota to extradite ICE agent Christian Castro from Texas. A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer who was charged in connection with shooting someone in Minnesota earlier this year was released from lockup in Texas on Thursday.

A judge on Wednesday declined to take action to prevent the man's release and force Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to send the individual back to Minnesota. Minnesota officials have been pushing to have the man held as they fight for his extradition in the Hennepin County case.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced in May that Castro was "being charged with four counts of assault in the second degree and one count of falsely reporting a crime."

"Mr. Castro fired his service weapon at the front door of a home knowing there were people who had just run inside that presented absolutely no harm to him or anyone else," Moriarty asserted, saying the bullet hit Julio Sosa-Celis in the leg and eventually lodged "in the wall of a child's bedroom."

Christian Castro was released from Texas custody on Aug. 27, 2026. (Cameron County Sheriff's Office)

U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez, Jr.'s Wednesday order denying a temporary restraining order declared, "In May, the State of Minnesota charged Castro with various crimes based on that incident. When authorities in the State of Texas arrested Castro in late May, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz initiated the process under the Extradition Act of 1793 and the Uniform Criminal Extradition Act to secure Castro’s extradition to Minnesota."

"Under the UCEA, Castro can be detained on the strength of the Minnesota warrant only until August 27, 2026. On August 18, having not received a definitive answer, Minnesota filed this action, alleging that Governor Abbott 'has refused' to sign a rendition warrant, violating the Extradition Clause of the United States Constitution, the Extradition Act, and the UCEA," the order stated.

title: Free climber stranded on Georgia rock face calls 911, prompting dramatic rescue by firefighter
summary: Drone video captures firefighter Will Roper rappelling down Mount Yonah's cliff face to reach a free climber stranded on a tiny ledge 260 feet up.
story: The climber was stuck on the side of Mount Yonah, a 3,166-foot mountain ridge in the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest in North Georgia.
A free climber who called 911 after becoming stranded on a Georgia cliff face was rescued Tuesday by a firefighter who rappelled down to reach him.
The climber, who hasn't been identified by authorities, was stuck on the west face of Mount Yonah, a 3,166-foot mountain ridge in the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest in North Georgia.
According to White County Public Safety officials, the man called 911 at around 7 p.m. to report that he was unable to safely climb up or down the mountain.
Authorities used a drone to locate the man, who was standing on a 20" by 20" ledge approximately 260 feet up the mountain.
11 VISITORS TRAPPED AS DANGEROUS FLASH FLOODING TEARS THROUGH ICONIC NATIONAL PARK
White County firefighter Will Roper maneuvers underneath the free climber, who was stranded on Georgia's Mount Yonah on the night of Aug. 25, 2026. (White County Public Safety)

White County firefighter Will Roper rappelled down the mountain to reach the man. Drone video showed Roper maneuvering beneath him before securing him in a harness and clipping him to the rope. The climber was then hoisted to the top of the mountain.
The entire rescue operation took about 42 minutes, officials said.
Roper told FOX 5 Atlanta said this was the first time he's had to rescue someone on a mountain.
Firefighter Will Roper goes over the edge of Mount Yonah on Aug. 25 to rescue a stranded climber. (White County Public Safety)
FIREFIGHTERS, POLICE PULL YOUNG WOMAN FROM SEWAGE-FILLED RAVINE AFTER DAYS TRAPPED IN 104-DEGREE HEAT
"I've done a lot with dummies and a lot with other firefighters in training, but that's the first time that I've ever done it, kind of in the heat of the moment with a live subject," Roper said.
"It was a little nerve-racking going over the edge," he added.
Roper said the climber was strikingly calm, telling FOX 5 he jokingly asked him: "Have you been rescued before? You're pretty good at this."
Will Roper and the free climber are seen on the west face of Mount Yonah during the Aug. 25 rescue operation. (White County Public Safety)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The climber told Roper that he had experience with Mount Yonah but simply picked the wrong route and got stuck.
"I've been on kind of a high since then, just to have the first rescue," Roper said, adding that he was glad to be able to help someone using his technical training.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: USS George Washington captain says morale is high for new Mideast mission
summary: Ship's commanding office says morale is high on the USS George Washington as it replaces the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East.
story: Operations and scenes on the mess deck on the aircraft carrier, USS George Washington, filmed in the Arabian Sea, August 2026. (Video US Navy via DVIDS.)
FIRST ON FOX: Morale is said to be high as the aircraft carrier the USS George Washington has arrived in the Arabian Sea near the vital Strait of Hormuz and close to Iran.

The carrier, CVN 73, has replaced the USS Abraham Lincoln. Fresh from a visit to Vietnam three weeks ago, the 5,000 sailors aboard this mobile airfield, base to approximately nine operational squadrons of advanced strike fighters, electronic attack planes and helicopter assets are, according to senior officers, ready and willing to carry out their new mission.

"Morale aboard USS George Washington remains high among our sailors," Capt. Nicholas DeLeo, the ship’s Commanding Officer, told Fox News Digital. He added "I see this as I walk the deck plates, seeing them take pride in their work — whether conducting flight operations, maintaining our systems or supporting one another on the ship. The dedication and teamwork I see across the ship is outstanding, and that spirit keeps us ready and resilient."
CENTCOM COMMANDER TOUTS USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN MENTAL HEALTH RECORD AFTER MORE THAN 260 DAYS WITHOUT PORT CALL

Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN 73) conducts routine operations while underway in the Arabian Sea, Aug. 22, 2026. George Washington is deployed to the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations to support maritime security and stability in the Middle East.  (U.S. Navy photo)

The George Washington, a Nimitz-class carrier, is the flagship of Carrier Strike Group (CSG) 5, and is reported to be accompanied by several warships, including the guided missile cruiser USS Robert Smalls (CG 62) and the guided missile destroyer USS Shoup (DDG 86).

Commander of Carrier Strike Group Five, Rear Adm. Jeff Heames, told Fox News Digital "The teams aboard USS George Washington and Carrier Strike Group Five are ready, determined, and resourced for sustained operations. Our Sailors understand the importance of the mission and continue to execute with precision and professionalism every day."

With the carrier group now operating in the Middle East, it falls under US Central Command (CENTCOM). The command’s former Commander, Gen. Joseph Votel, (Ret.), recently told Fox News’ America Reports about the George Washington’s expected mission, saying "Being able to continue to have credible military capability in the Middle East is really important, so the arrival of the George Washington is I think a good example of that."
Votel continued, "We’re going to have to be prepared, because this is probably going to take some time, to continue to bring forces into the region, we want them to be at a high level of readiness."
IRAN WAR THRUSTS DIEGO GARCIA INTO SPOTLIGHT AS OFFICIAL CALLS US MILITARY BASE ‘INTEGRAL’

Flight operations continue, both day and night. Launching into the skies off Iran from the George Washington, aircraft based on board are reported to be F/A-18E/F Super Hornet multirole strike fighters, F-35C Lightning II fifth-generation stealth multirole fighters, EA-18G Growler electronic warfare aircraft and E-2D Advanced Hawkeye airborne early warning and control.
Also onboard are said to be MH-60S Seahawk & MH-60R Seahawk multi-mission helicopters for anti-submarine warfare and search-and-rescue.

This past week, a historic landing on the George Washington. Navy Lt. Steven Frazier, a pilot from Strike Fighter Squadron 147, the Argonauts, made the 200,000th trap - landing on the ship in an F-35C Lightning II fighter jet, with his stealth fighter caught by a thick, steel arresting gear cable with the jet’s tail hook.

In a laid-back understatement that could have come straight out of the movie ‘Top Gun’, Lt. Frazier said, "It's a good feeling for me to know that once I leave, I can come back to the aircraft carrier and trap". The carrier can land one aircraft on deck per minute, and typically lands 70 aircraft a day.
IRAN WAR FORCES AMERICA TO CONFRONT THE STRATEGIC COST OF DETERRING CHINA

An F/A-18 Super Hornet, attached to Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 27, prepares for takeoff aboard Nimitz-class aircraft carrier the USS George Washington in the Arabian Sea Aug. 21 2026.  (NAVCENT Public Affairs)

Attention to mission is evident throughout the ship. On the bridge, Assistant Navigator Elizabeth Wayne told the ship’s communication team, "all of the time when we are navigating, we are focused outside of the ship on anything that could pose a hazard or a threat to the ship."

Wayne continued, "When we are in special evolution, when we are conducting flight operations, the most important thing is to ensure we are lock step with (the) airboss, the captain, the command duty officer underway, everybody needs to be on the same page to execute that safely."

As it arrived in the Middle East, Russia tried to suggest the food on the carrier was not good. Russia Today (RT) posted what are believed to be AI-generated photos of poor rations on board. However, from the videos seen by Fox News Digital of great food and even a café below decks, the truth appears to be very different. Victoria Marc, Culinary Specialist 2nd Class, talked to the communications team on the carrier, noting that "throughout the day and into the night, our sailors have all sorts of food and drink options available to them."

Marc added, "Sailors have the opportunity to eat three meals a day, plus the night rations. Our 150 cooks work 24 hours to prepare and serve 15,000 meals a day to ensure our sailors are well-fed. From the mess deck throughout the day, there’s always something there where people feel fueled and ready for the fight."

And the Navy intends keeping it this way. Earlier this week, CENTCOM published images of the George Washington being replenished at sea. Navy images show the ship being resupplied twice in four days this past week, an average of 2,000 pallets of supplies including fresh food and ammunition winched by helicopter from a nearby supply ship.
Fuel for the carrier’s aircraft is also transferred ship-to-ship. The carrier is nuclear-powered, so the ship itself will not need refueling at sea.
WHO CONTROLS THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ RIGHT NOW? HERE'S WHAT THE SHIP TRAFFIC ACTUALLY SHOWS

Kaiser (T-AO-187), delivers supplies to Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN 73) during a replenishment-at-sea evolution in the Arabian Sea, Aug. 22, 2026. George Washington is deployed to the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations to support maritime security and stability in the Middle East.  (US Navy photo)
More history this week – under the headline "Shoutout to our Shipbuilders!!", the ship’s communications team posted "40 years ago on August 25, 1986, the keel for USS George Washington was laid."

Today in the Arabian Sea, that keel supports the 5,000 men and women and their array of air firepower, as they stand at the coalface of the Middle East conflict, ready – and willing – to carry out their mission.

title: Switzerland rave shooting kills 1, injures 5 as police hunt those responsible
summary: A 22-year-old woman was killed and five others wounded at the Aarau Rave in northern Switzerland as police launch a large-scale search operation.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A 22-year-old woman was killed and five other people were wounded in a shooting early Sunday at a rave in northern Switzerland, authorities said, as police launched a large-scale search for those responsible.

The shooting happened in the Schachen area of Aarau, the capital of Switzerland’s Aargau canton, where the "Aarau Rave VOL. 7" was being held at a horse-racing track, according to Swiss broadcaster SRF.

Aargau cantonal police said the woman died from her injuries at the scene. Four men and another woman, all between the ages of 24 and 27, were taken to hospitals with injuries ranging from minor to serious.
All six victims are residents of Switzerland, police said.
ONE DEAD, 6 INJURED AFTER GUNFIRE ERUPTS AT UNSANCTIONED CALIFORNIA PARTY THAT DREW HUNDREDS: SHERIFF
Police officers patrol a street in downtown Aarau, Switzerland Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026, following a shooting at a rave. (Michael Buholzer/Keystone via AP)

Police spokesman Pascal Wenzel told SRF that authorities were alerted to the shooting shortly after 2:30 a.m. The event had been scheduled to end at 2 a.m., according to SRF, which cited information from the organizers’ website.
Authorities said the perpetrator or perpetrators remained unidentified and that possible motives and the circumstances surrounding the shooting were still unclear.
Police officers block a street near the Schachen horse racing track in Aarau following a shooting at a rave event near Aarau, Switzerland Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026. (Michael Buholzer/Keystone via AP)

A large area surrounding the horse-racing track, swimming pool and nearby sports field was cordoned off as police searched the area. Authorities also increased their presence elsewhere in Aarau as a precaution and urged members of the public to stay away.
ALL 12 VICTIMS STABLE AFTER SHOOTING NEAR FESTIVAL AS TOLEDO POLICE PURSUE MULTIPLE LEADS
Armed police officers patrol near the Schachen horse racing track in Aarau following a shooting during a rave event near Aarau, Switzerland, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026. (Michael Buholzer/Keystone via AP)

The response included police officers, firefighters and several emergency medical services, according to SRF. The broadcaster reported that a cantonal disaster-response unit, the Argus police special unit and a Swiss military Super Puma helicopter were also involved.
Police in neighboring Germany were also assisting with the search as part of routine cross-border cooperation, a spokesman in Freiburg told the German news agency dpa, according to SRF.
Police appealed to witnesses to provide investigators with videos or photographs from the event and established an information line for relatives and eyewitnesses.
Armed police officers patrol near the Schachen horse racing track in Aarau following a shooting during a rave event near Aarau, Switzerland, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026. (Michael Buholzer/Keystone via AP)

Swiss DJ Tekibo, who performed at the rave, later wrote on Instagram that what happened was "absolutely heartbreaking" and said raves should be places of freedom and safety. He also said he had lost an "important friend," though SRF reported that it was not clear whom he was referring to.

Police said their investigation and search operation remained ongoing.

title: Muslim jail gangs said to force conversions on prisoners in UK: 'Jihadist training camps’
summary: Reports of forced conversions in British prisons have renewed alarm over extremist gang influence. Officials say faith-based coercion will not be tolerated.
story: Rep. Brandon Gill, a member of the House Oversight Committee, condemns the alleged cover-up of widespread U.K. grooming gang crimes, primarily involving Muslim immigrants targeting working-class British children.
Radical Muslim inmates are said to be forcing other prisoners — mostly White British men — to convert to Islam in some of the U.K.'s prisons, according to British media reports this week.

The problem of Muslim gangs in the nation's prisons has become progressively worse since Britain's Sky News first reported in 2013 that "British inmates are being bullied into converting to Islam while in jail" while noting that the "Prison Officers Association says it is symptomatic of the growing power and influence of Muslim gangs in prison."
This week, Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary of the opposition Conservative party, has urged the left-of-center Labour government to root out forced conversions.

Timothy posted on X Tuesday, "Islamist gangs control many of our prisons. Conversion to Islam is the only way to stay safe from them. I obtained data showing 1 in 5 Muslim prisoners are white. That’s four times higher than in the general population. This cannot continue."

A prison guard walks past a sign to the prison mosque inside Wandsworth prison. HMP Wandsworth in South West London was built in 1851 and is one of the largest prisons in Western Europe. It has a capacity of 1,456 prisoners. (Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures Ltd./Corbis via Getty Images))

He told the U.K.'s Daily Telegraph, "We know that experts have warned repeatedly about forced conversions taking place behind bars, driven by Islamic gangs," Timothy said. "We need to be honest that something is not right here – Labour must urgently investigate and stamp out forced conversions in prison."

A press release from the U.K. Ministry of Justice stated, "Most prisons show no evidence of gang-based extremism. We have also banned terrorist prisoners from holding positions of authority in corporate worship, e.g. leading the call to prayer, and clamped down on material found in prisons that could be used to spread harmful ideologies of justice."
According to Nile Gardiner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation, this growing trend is having a detrimental effect on the country's prison system.

"It is an absolutely outrageous state of affairs in the British prison system. This also poses a very significant national security risk for the United Kingdom. The British government appears to have lost control over its prisons, which have become jihadist training camps," Gardiner, who advised Lady Thatcher, told Fox News Digital.
He added that "urgent actions need to be taken" in response to "the level of forced Islamization in British jails."
UK ASYLUM SEEKERS COULD HAVE TO PAY GOVERNMENT $13K BEFORE APPLYING FOR SETTLEMENT

Prisoners return from their jobs to their wings for lunch at Wandsworth prison. HMP Wandsworth in South West London was built in 1851 and is one of the largest prisons in Western Europe.  (Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures Ltd./Corbis via Getty Images)

The number of incarcerated Muslims has its origins in a defective British immigration policy, said Gardiner. According to The Telegraph, "the number of Muslim prisoners in jails in England and Wales has also increased and accounts for nearly one in five (18%) of the prison population, despite making up 6.5% of the general population."

"It is very clear that large-scale Islamic migration into the United Kingdom is having a direct impact on crime and public safety in the United Kingdom," Gardiner told Fox News Digital. "And the growing Islamization of Britain carries with it immense risks for British national security and crime. The inflow of Islamic migrants is a real threat to Britain’s future."

A British Union flag flies from a souvenir stall near the Houses of Parliament in London Oct. 27, 2025. (Jason Alden/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Bloom had previously told GB News there are some very good (Muslim) chaplains and excellent practices in prison, but "there is also, I think fair to say, that a number of prisons there are very large and aggressive Islamist gangs … where evidence was given to me and my review where Korans were put on the bed of incoming inmates with the very clear indication: Convert or get hurt. But even by the standards of the most amazing, you know, revivals, religious conversions, there is something going on in prisons because we are seeing the most incredible number of people converting, particularly to Islam, in a way that defies logic.

title: Death toll from mudslides, flooding at Nepal-China border climbs past 670; nearly 3,000 missing
summary: Nepal's flood and mudslide death toll reaches more than 670 with nearly 3,000 missing as rain and fog halt search and rescue operations in the disaster zone.
story: Rescue crews in Nepal are searching for hundreds of people missing after devastating floods, including dozens of Americans still unaccounted for. Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports on the urgent recovery effort on ‘America Reports.’
The death toll from the devastating floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border has risen to at least 676 people as rescue operations stall amid poor weather.
After Nepali authorities updated their figures Saturday, the combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 676 dead and nearly 3,000 people missing, according to The Associated Press.
Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing, while Nepal’s disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 669 with 2,426 people missing.
Experts believe Wednesday's mudslides and flash flooding across Nepal and China's Tibet region were caused by a large chunk of ice breaking off a glacier and falling into the Lhende Khola River.
MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF

Rescue operations in the main disaster zone have been complicated by damaged roads and difficulty establishing communication and look only to get more difficult as intermittent rain is expected through the weekend.
"Search and rescue operations have been temporarily halted because it is raining, and the weather is foggy," Narendra Pariyar, a top official for Nepal's Rasuwa district, told Reuters.
A man holds an umbrella as he stands in front of damaged buildings after flash floods and a mudslide in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, Aug. 29, 2026. (Reuters/Athit Perawongmetha)

While Nepalese authorities have stressed they don't need countries to send people to help with general search and rescue, they did request that China send tunnel experts because up to 100 people are still trapped in a mud-filled hydropower plant tunnel.
ARMY BLACK HAWKS AIRLIFT 200-PLUS STRANDED CAMPERS AS MISSOURI FLOODS TRIGGER MORE 350 RESCUES

"We have already made requests for such specialized services and technical assistance in areas where we don't have enough expertise and technical know-how," Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Reuters.
China dispatched five such workers from Tibet by helicopter to assist, according to the country's state-affiliated Xinhua news agency.

Chinese rescue workers arrive at Maithili Barrack, an army training center that serves as a primary base for airlifting survivors after deadly flash floods and a mudslide in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal, Aug. 29, 2026. (Reuters/Athit Perawongmetha)
COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION
Dramatic video showed the rescue of one such person as authorities from Nepal worked to drag the man out of the mud deluge.

Though impending rainstorms are likely to make rescue operations more difficult, officials say a previous threat from a lake that had formed on the border between Nepal and Tibet has substantially subsided.
MASSIVE GARBAGE HEAP COLLAPSES ONTO HOMES, KILLING AT LEAST 30 AS RESCUERS SEARCH FOR SURVIVORS
The lake had been overflowing into the Lhende Khola River, risking further flooding, but that risk had gone down by Saturday, according to Chinese officials.

A satellite image shows one of two lakes at the site of the glacial collapse in the border area between Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China, Aug. 28, 2026. (SPOT CNES 2026, Distribution Airbus DS/Handout via Reuters)
Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle estimated the country will need over $4 billion to rebuild after the disaster.

"This is just an estimate. Loss and damage is being assessed," he told Reuters.
Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Trapped Nepali workers pulled from hydropower tunnel after catastrophic flooding
summary: Video from Nepal's Prime Minister's Office shows rescue workers pulling trapped citizens through a mud-saturated hydropower plant tunnel in Rasuwa.
story: Dramatic video shows rescue workers in Nepal dragging a trapped person through the mud in a hydroplant tunnel after a deadly mudslide swept through the region. Credit: Reuters.
Stunning video shows rescue workers in Nepal dragging trapped citizens out of the mud in a hydropower plant tunnel after the devastating mudslide that has left over 1,000 people missing.
The video, released by Nepal’s Prime Minister’s Office on Friday, shows a series of rescue workers pulling trapped people through a tunnel that’s been saturated with mud.

In a post on Facebook, the Prime Minister’s Office said it had rescued 350 people from the tunnel but that efforts continue to evacuate more than 100 people still trapped. The post also added that workers had moved another 533 residents to safety from flooded areas.
The rescue operation is intended to save people after a disastrous mudslide struck the valley in the Rasuwa district in northern Nepal, also affecting neighboring Chinese province Tibet.
TERRIFYING VIDEO CAPTURES PEOPLE FLEEING INCOMING MUDSLIDE AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER

Rescuers evacuate a person from a tunnel of a hydropower project, in the aftermath of flash floods and a mudslide, in Rasuwa, Nepal, in this still image from handout video released August 28, 2026. (PMO Nepal/Handout via Reuters)
At least 538 people have been confirmed dead in Nepal, according to the most recent estimate from the Nepal National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and the Nepal Police.
MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF
People unaccounted for on the Nepal side now number up to 1,924, according to The Associated Press.
Chinese authorities also report that, on the Chinese side of the border in Tibet, which was also affected by the deluge and ensuing mudslide, five people were confirmed dead with another 558 missing.
Aftermath of flash floods and mudslide at Trishuli Bazaar army training centre in Nuwakot, Nepal, August 28, 2026. (REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas)
AMERICAN HIKER VANISHES ON TROPICAL TREK AS FLASH FLOODS, MUDSLIDES TURN JUNGLE GETAWAY INTO DESPERATE SEARCH
Of the many missing people are approximately 90 Americans, according to the U.S. State Department.

President Donald Trump commented on the disaster Thursday, telling reporters, "That was a brutal... that was mud and water. It’s a mixture that nobody’s ever seen anything quite like that, where very powerful, strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks."
A 7.8 MAGNITUDE QUAKE IN THE PHILIPPINES KILLS AT LEAST 32, COLLAPSES BUILDINGS AND SPARKS TSUNAMI
The uniquely devastating natural disaster was likely caused by a giant ice rock that crashed into the Lhende Khola River after an earthquake, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).

"On Wednesday morning (local time), 26 August 2026, a catastrophic debris flow and flood was likely triggered by a glacial collapse in Langtang National Park, Nepal, near the border with China," the USGS said in a post on its website.
A survivor is transported to a safer place in a JCB following a flash flood at Trishuli in Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 26, 2026. (REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY)
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PLEDGES $150M IN AID, DEPLOYS NAVY WARSHIPS AFTER DEADLY VENEZUELA EARTHQUAKES

"This debris flow and flooding travelled nearly 100 km and impacted populated areas downstream along the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi Rivers, including Gyirong Port, China. Preliminary media reports and imagery analysis indicate many buildings and infrastructure have likely been buried or destroyed, including a vital highway connecting China and Nepal," the post added.
Fox News Digital contacted the Nepalese Foreign Ministry and the U.S. State Department for further comment.

title: Norway's King Harald dies peacefully at 89, son Crown Prince Haakon to succeed him
summary: Norway's King Harald died peacefully at Oslo University Hospital at age 89, with Crown Prince Haakon set to succeed him as the nation mourns.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Norway's King Harald died Friday at 89, the Royal House of Norway announced.
"It is with deep grief that we announce that His Majesty King Harald has passed away," the royal palace said in a statement.
"King Harald died peacefully at Oslo University Hospital Rikshospitalet Friday 28 August at 6:35 AM," the statement continued.
NORWAY RAISES SECURITY CONCERNS OVER MANHATTAN-SIZED ARCTIC LAND SALE AS TENSIONS RISE
Norway's King Harald died Friday at 89, the Royal House of Norway announced. (Reuters)
Harald, who was Europe's oldest living monarch, was hospitalized with a blood infection on Aug. 17.
He had previously received a pacemaker after falling ill during a vacation in Malaysia in 2024.
Harald announced he would be drawing down his number of public appearances that same year.

Her Majesty Queen Sonja of Norway, left, and His Majesty King Harald of Norway attend the Norwegian Constitution Day with the children's parade at the Royal Palace on May 17, 2026, in Oslo, Norway. (Per Ole Hagen/Getty Images)

The monarch had served as Norway's head of state since 1991. He was Norway's first royal heir to be born in the country in more than 500 years. In 1905, after Norway gained its independence from Sweden, Harald's grandfather, King Haakon VII, became the first king of an independent Norwegian state since 1387.
Harald was viewed as a reformer and advocated for his fellow European royals to continue a trend towards openness with the public.
"If you've opened the gate it's very difficult to close it again," he told Reuters. "I'm not sure I'd want to close it. So far so good, as far as I'm concerned."

King Harald V of Norway is seen on Oct. 4, 2022, as he visits Flesberg and Lampeland, Norway. Norway's King Harald V, Europe's oldest reigning monarch, died on Aug. 28, 2026, at the age of 89, the royal palace announced. (Terje Pedersen / NTB / AFP via Getty Images)

When the Nazis invaded Norway in 1940, Harald's mother fled with him, first to neutral Sweden, then to the United States, where they briefly lived in the White House after then-President Franklin Delano Roosevelt offered the pair safe haven.
Harald, his mother and his sisters soon moved to Bethesda, Maryland and would often meet with Roosevelt, who Harald said was like a grandfather to him.
Then-Prince Harald of Norway plays with Franklin D. Roosevelt's Scottish terrier, Fala, at Laura Delano's home in Rhinebeck, New York on Sept. 26, 1944. (CORBIS/Corbis via Getty Images)
Harald's son, Crown Prince Haakon, 53, will succeed him and take the name King Haakon VIII.

Haakon and his wife, who will become Queen Mette-Marit, have been embroiled in scandal since it was revealed she exchanged emails with and had multiple meetings with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
CROWN PRINCESS METTE-MARIT OF NORWAY SAYS SHE REGRETS HER TIES TO JEFFREY EPSTEIN
Mette-Marit said she regrets her ties to the deceased billionaire and claimed she had no knowledge of his sordid past while communicating with him.

Crown Princess Mette-Marit of Norway, Crown Prince Haakon of Norway and Prince Daniel of Sweden watch a performance at Fryshuset Foundation on May 3, 2022, in Stockholm, Sweden.  (Michael Campanella / Getty Images)

Additionally, Mette-Marit's son, Marius Borg Høiby, who she had from a previous marriage, was convicted of several charges of rape and domestic violence in June. He was sentenced to four years in prison, and both he and prosecutors are appealing the sentence.

title: Russia threatens strikes on UK military targets, ‘catastrophic consequences’ over Ukraine
summary: Russia threatened to strike British military targets inside and outside Ukraine after Moscow accused Kyiv of using Storm Shadow missiles against Donetsk.
story: Home-produced weapon targets Russian ammunition hub, marking a leap in Kyiv’s strike capability. (Den Shtillerman via X/East2West.)

Russia warned Thursday that it could strike British military targets inside and outside Ukraine if Kyiv uses long-range British cruise missiles against targets deep inside Russian territory, according to reports.
This came a day after Moscow accused Ukraine of striking a shopping center in Russian-controlled Donetsk with British Storm Shadow missiles, wounding civilians, including children.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Thursday that Britain was "one step away" from becoming legally complicit in what she described as civilian-targeted "terrorism," warning that failure to change course would bring "catastrophic consequences," Reuters reported.
US ALLY ON PUTIN’S DOORSTEP BRACES FOR WAR AS RUSSIA TENSIONS TAKE OMINOUS TURN
Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova attends the annual news conference held by Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov Jan. 14, 2025, in Moscow. (Evgenia Novozhenina/Reuters)

"We have repeatedly warned that any British military installations and equipment in Ukraine and beyond its borders could be targeted in response to Ukrainian strikes on Russian territory carried out using British weapons," Zakharova said at a news briefing in Moscow.
She urged British leaders to "immediately, in the most resolute and unequivocal manner, abandon the hostile, aggressive line" to prevent the conflict from escalating to an "entirely new level."

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Ukraine Aug. 24 for Independence Day, when he announced that a defense contractor could release classified information about British components used in the long-range SCALP cruise missile as Ukraine and France seek to establish assembly lines in Ukraine, according to the U.K. government.
PUTIN 'PANICKED' AS DEFIANT UKRAINE MARKS INDEPENDENCE DAY UNDER RUSSIAN BOMBARDMENT

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Ukraine Aug. 24 for Independence Day, when he announced that a defense contractor could release classified information about British components used in the long-range cruise missiles. (Getty Images )
The SCALP missile, the French version of Britain's Storm Shadow, can strike targets more than 155 miles away.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the U.K. was "participating in the war" and "pouring fuel on the fire."

A spokesperson for Britain's Ministry of Defense told Reuters London stood "shoulder to shoulder" with Ukraine and was committed to providing the equipment that Kyiv needed "to defend itself against (President Vladimir) Putin's illegal invasion."
"Russia should be in no doubt about the resolve of this government to stand against Russian aggression in Ukraine and against the U.K. and our allies," the spokesperson said.
UK'S BURNHAM NAMES TRUMP CRITIC ED MILIBAND FOREIGN SECRETARY; EX-THATCHER AIDE BRANDS PICK 'DISASTROUS'

Russia also warned Britain Aug. 17 that it would pay a "price" after The Times reported Aug. 15 that British-made drones supplied to Ukraine were used to strike military and industrial targets inside Russia for the very first time. (Getty Images)
During his Kyiv visit, Burnham also hit back at Moscow, condemning Russia's "outrageous threats" and asserting that Britain's support for Ukraine would not waver.

Russia also warned Britain Aug. 17 that it would pay a "price" after The Times reported Aug. 15 that British-made drones supplied to Ukraine were used to strike military and industrial targets inside Russia for the very first time.
Britain's Ministry of Defense did not confirm whether British drones had been used in the strikes.
Zakharova made the remarks as President Donald Trump downplayed concerns about a broader war, telling Axios in a phone interview Thursday he was not concerned Russia would attack a NATO member.
US MILITARY PLANE LANDS IN MOSCOW, WITH KREMLIN CLAIMING IT HAS NO INFORMATION: REPORT
Footage shows the launch of Ukraine’s homegrown long-range "Flamingo" cruise missiles during a strike on Russian military infrastructure. (East2West)
Sergei Naryshkin, head of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service, known as the SVR, confirmed Thursday that he met with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Moscow earlier this week, Reuters reported.

Naryshkin characterized the meeting as routine, saying they discussed issues within the scope of their intelligence services, according to Reuters.
Trump similarly described Ratcliffe's trip as "semi-routine," according to Axios.
